claude-code.name: Claude Code
claude-code.setup: Replace tab_replace_with_your_key with your saved key, then run this command in a terminal with Claude Code installed.
claude-code.note: This adds a local Claude Code connection. Keep the key out of shared project files and repositories.
claude-code.verify: Run claude mcp list, then open Claude Code and use /mcp to inspect tabdo. Ask it to list the tables your key can read.
claude-code.short: Run the command, then inspect tabdo with /mcp in Claude Code.
claude-code.setupGenerated: Run the full command above in a terminal with Claude Code installed.

claude-remote.name: Claude web / Desktop
claude-remote.setup: In Claude, open Customize → Connectors → Add custom connector. Enter the server name and URL below. Choose No sign in under Authentication, then add the Authorization value under Request headers.
claude-remote.note: No sign in skips OAuth; the Bearer key is still required. Use a public HTTPS endpoint. Team or Enterprise users may need an owner to add the connector in organization settings. If Request headers is unavailable, use a client that supports Bearer headers.
claude-remote.verify: Finish adding the connector, enable tabdo for the conversation through Connectors, then ask it to list your authorized tables.
claude-remote.short: Choose No sign in in your custom connector and add the Bearer value under Request headers. A public HTTPS URL is required.
claude-remote.setupGenerated: In Claude, open Customize → Connectors → Add custom connector. Enter the name and URL above, choose No sign in under Authentication, then add the Authorization header and its Bearer value under Request headers.

codex.name: Codex
codex.setupTitle: Set the key and add the server
codex.setup: Replace the placeholder with your saved key. Keep TABDO_MCP_KEY available in the environment that launches Codex. Run the command in your terminal.
codex.note: The server configuration refers to the environment variable. Keep its value private and out of shared files and shell history.
codex.verify: Run codex mcp list, then open Codex and use /mcp to inspect tabdo. Ask it to list the tables your key can read.
codex.short: Run the commands, then launch Codex from the same terminal environment and inspect tabdo with /mcp.
codex.setupGenerated: Run the commands above and launch Codex from the same terminal so it can read TABDO_MCP_KEY.

cursor.name: Cursor
cursor.setup: Add this entry to your personal ~/.cursor/mcp.json. Replace the placeholder with your saved key, save the file, then restart Cursor. Merge with existing servers if needed.
cursor.note: Keep real keys out of shared .cursor/mcp.json files and repositories. This connection uses Streamable HTTP with a Bearer header.
cursor.verify: In Customize → MCPs, enable tabdo and check that its tools appear in chat. Ask it to list your authorized tables. Use MCP Logs in the Output panel to investigate failures.
cursor.short: Save to your personal ~/.cursor/mcp.json, merge with existing servers, then restart Cursor.
cursor.setupGenerated: Save the full configuration above to your personal ~/.cursor/mcp.json, merging existing servers if needed, then restart Cursor.

grok-bot.name: Grok Bot
grok-bot.setup: Where your Grok account offers custom MCP servers, add tabdo with the URL below and type Remote HTTPS (Streamable HTTP). In the secure HTTP headers form, enter Authorization and its Bearer value. Leave OAuth Client ID and Client Secret empty.
grok-bot.note: If your version only offers OAuth and has no secure HTTP headers form, this connection is unavailable. Use a client that supports Bearer headers. Grok Bot needs a public HTTPS URL; never paste the key into chat or a URL.
grok-bot.verify: Open Connect apps and add the connector if prompted. Attach tabdo to a task with @, then ask it to list your authorized tables.
grok-bot.short: Use only if your client offers a secure HTTP headers form. If only OAuth is available, choose another client.
grok-bot.setupGenerated: If your client provides custom MCP and a secure HTTP headers form, enter the public URL and Authorization value above. This configuration does not provide OAuth sign-in.
